title: Contains Duplicate
problem: Given an integer array nums, return true if any value appears more than once in the array, otherwise return false.
hint: A brute force solution would be to check every element against every other element in the array. This would be an O(n^2) solution. Can you think of a better way?
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(n) space.

title: Valid Anagram
problem: Given two strings s and t, return true if the two strings are anagrams of each other, else return false.
hint: A brute force solution would be to sort the given strings and check for their equality. This would be an O(nlogn + mlogm) solution. Can you think of a better way without sorting the strings?
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Minimum Window Substring
problem: Given two strings s and t, return the minimum window in s which contains all the characters of t.
hint: Try using two pointers and a hash map to expand and contract the window.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(m) space.

title: Palindromic Substrings
problem: Given a string s, return the number of palindromic substrings in it.
hint: Try expanding around every possible center.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n^2) time and O(1) space.

title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
problem: Design an algorithm to serialize and deserialize a binary tree.
hint: You can use BFS or DFS traversal; remember to handle null children.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(n) space.

title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
problem: Given preorder and inorder traversal of a tree, construct the binary tree.
hint: Root is the first element in preorder and split inorder by root.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(n) space.

title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal II
problem: Given the root of a binary tree, return the bottom-up level order traversal of its nodes' values.
hint: Gather levels top-down and reverse at the end.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(n) space.

title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
problem: Given a binary search tree, find the k-th smallest element in it.
hint: Try using in-order traversal for BST.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(h + k) time and O(h) space.

title: Merge k Sorted Lists
problem: Merge k sorted linked lists and return it as one sorted list.
hint: Use a min-heap or merge pairwise recursively.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(N log k) time and O(N) space, where N is the total number of nodes.

title: Clone Graph
problem: Given a reference node to a graph, return a deep copy (clone) of the graph.
hint: Use DFS or BFS with a map to track copied nodes.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(n) space, where n is the # of nodes.

title: Graph Valid Tree
problem: Given n nodes labeled 0 to n-1 and a list of edges, determine if it's a valid tree.
hint: Check for cycles and that all nodes are connected.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(n) space.

title: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph
problem: Given n nodes and a list of undirected edges, return the number of connected components.
hint: Use DFS/BFS to visit each component.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n + e) time and O(n) space, where e = #edges.

title: Word Search
problem: Given an m x n board and a word, determine if the word exists in the grid by moving horizontally or vertically.
hint: Try DFS for each letter and mark visited cells.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(m*n*L) time and O(L) space, where L = word length.

title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
problem: Given an m x n matrix, return list of grid coordinates where water can flow to both Pacific and Atlantic.
hint: Reverse the flow: start from oceans and mark reachable cells with DFS/BFS.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(m*n) time and O(m*n) space.

title: Alien Dictionary
problem: Given a sorted dictionary of an alien language, return a possible order of the letters.
hint: Create a graph of precedence and use topological sort.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(c) time and O(c) space, where c = total characters.

title: Course Schedule II
problem: Given numCourses and prerequisites, return the ordering of courses you should take to finish all.
hint: Topological sort helps if no cycles; otherwise, it's impossible.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(V + E) time and O(V) space.

title: Word Ladder
problem: Given two words (beginWord and endWord), and a dictionary, return the number of steps in the shortest sequence to transform beginWord to endWord.
hint: Use BFS, changing one letter at a time.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(N*M^2) time and O(N*M) space, where N = word list size, M = word length.

title: Combination Sum
problem: Given an array of distinct integers candidates and an integer target, return all unique combinations of candidates that sum to target.
hint: Use backtracking to build up solutions.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(2^n) time and O(target) space.

title: Permutations
problem: Given a collection of distinct integers, return all possible permutations.
hint: Use backtracking and swap elements to build each permutation.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n!) time and O(n) space.

title: Subsets
problem: Given an integer array nums, return all possible subsets (the power set).
hint: For each element, decide whether to include it or not. Use backtracking.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n*2^n) time and O(n*2^n) space.

title: Combination Sum II
problem: Given a collection of candidate numbers (candidates) and a target number (target), find all unique combinations where candidates may only be used once.
hint: Sort candidates, use backtracking, and skip duplicates to avoid same combinations.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(2^n) time and O(target) space.

title: Word Search II
problem: Given a 2D board and a list of words, find all words in the board.
hint: Use a Trie and DFS to improve search efficiency.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(N*L), N = board size, L = total length of words.

title: Sudoku Solver
problem: Write a program to solve a Sudoku puzzle by filling empty cells.
hint: Backtracking to fill each cell, check valid placement.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(9^m) time, where m is #empty cells.

title: N-Queens
problem: The n-queens puzzle is to place n queens on an n x n chessboard so that no two queens attack each other.
hint: Use backtracking with row, column, and diagonal constraints.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n!) time.

title: Graph Clone
problem: Clone an undirected graph. Each node contains a value and a list of its neighbors.
hint: Use DFS/BFS with a visited map.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(n) space.

title: Number of Islands
problem: Given a 2D grid map of '1's and '0's, count the number of islands.
hint: Use BFS or DFS to explore each island from a found '1'.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(mn) time and O(mn) space.

title: Flood Fill
problem: Given an image (2D array) and a starting pixel, flood fill the image using a new color.
hint: Use BFS or DFS to recolor all connected pixels.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(mn) time and O(mn) space.

title: Set Matrix Zeroes
problem: Given an m x n integer matrix, if an element is 0, set its entire row and column to 0.
hint: Can you do this in place? Try using extra space first, then reduce it.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(mn) time and O(1) extra space.

title: Spiral Matrix
problem: Given an m x n matrix, return all elements in spiral order.
hint: Keep track of the current bounds as you spiral over the matrix.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(mn) time and O(1) space.

title: Rotate Image
problem: You are given an n x n 2D matrix representing an image. Rotate the image by 90 degrees (clockwise), in place.
hint: Transpose, then reverse each row, or swap four elements in cycles directly.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n^2) time and O(1) space.

title: Group Anagrams
problem: Given an array of strings, group anagrams together.
hint: Sort each string and use as dictionary key.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n*k*log(k)) time where k is avg string length.

title: Maximum Subarray
problem: Given an integer array nums, find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum.
hint: Try modifying the running sum as you iterate (Kadane’s algorithm).
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Coin Change
problem: Given coins and an amount, compute the minimum number of coins to make the amount.
hint: Try dynamic programming, storing best answer for every amount up to target.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(amount * coins.length) time.

title: Climbing Stairs
problem: You are climbing a staircase. Each time you can take 1 or 2 steps. How many distinct ways can you climb to the top?
hint: Think of it as a Fibonacci recurrence (DP).
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
problem: Given an integer array nums, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
hint: Try DP; can you improve the naive O(n^2) approach?
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n^2) time or O(n log n) if optimized.

title: Longest Common Subsequence
problem: Given two strings, return the length of their longest common subsequence.
hint: Classic DP: use a 2D table where each cell depends on previous cells.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(mn) time and O(mn) space.

title: Word Break
problem: Given a string and a dictionary of words, determine if the string can be segmented into a space-separated sequence of dictionary words.
hint: Dynamic programming to check word breaks up to each index.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n^2) time and O(n) space.

title: House Robber
problem: Given a list of non-negative integers representing the amount of money in each house, determine the maximum amount of money you can rob without robbing adjacent houses.
hint: Think recursively: at each house, you can rob it or skip it. Use dynamic programming.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: House Robber II
problem: Similar to House Robber, but houses are arranged in a circle.
hint: Solve twice: once excluding the first house, once excluding the last.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Decode Ways
problem: Given a string containing only digits, determine the total number of ways to decode it.
hint: Use DP — the answer for a prefix depends on previous 1–2 digits.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(n) space.

title: Unique Paths
problem: A robot is located at the top-left corner of an m x n grid. How many unique paths are there to the bottom-right corner (only right and down)?
hint: Dynamic programming: each cell’s answer is the sum of the answers from the cell above and to the left.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(mn) time and O(mn) or O(n) space.

title: Jump Game
problem: Given an array of non-negative integers, each representing your maximum jump length per position, determine if you can reach the last index.
hint: Keep track of the furthest index you can reach as you iterate.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
problem: Given a rotated sorted array, search for a target value and return its index, or -1 if not found.
hint: Binary search with conditions for rotated halves.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(log n) time and O(1) space.

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
problem: Given a rotated sorted array, find the minimum element.
hint: Binary search to find the inflection point.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(log n) time and O(1) space.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array II
problem: Given a rotated sorted array that may contain duplicates, check if a target value exists in the array.
hint: Carefully handle duplicates and use binary search.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(log n) time (linear if many duplicates) and O(1) space.

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
problem: Given two sorted arrays nums1 and nums2, return the median of the two arrays.
hint: Binary search and divide-and-conquer can achieve logarithmic time.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(log(min(n, m))) time and O(1) space.

title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
problem: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the kth largest element in the array.
hint: Use a min heap of size k, or quickselect (partition algorithm).
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) average time and O(1) space.

title: Top K Frequent Elements
problem: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements.
hint: Bucket sort or heap based on frequencies.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(n) space.

title: Find K Closest Elements
problem: Given a sorted array and two integers k and x, return the k closest integers to x in the array.
hint: Binary search for the best left bound, then use a window.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(log(n-k) + k) time and O(k) space.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
problem: Given an array nums and an integer k, return the maximum value in each sliding window of size k.
hint: Try using a deque to keep track of the useful elements.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(k) space.

title: Subarray Sum Equals K
problem: Given an array of integers and an integer k, return the total number of subarrays whose sum equals k.
hint: Use a hashmap to track running sums seen so far.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(n) space.

title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
problem: Given an array of positive integers nums and an integer target, return the minimal length of a subarray sum ≥ target. If none, return 0.
hint: Try a sliding window approach, moving left pointer when current sum ≥ target.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Longest Substring with At Most K Distinct Characters
problem: Given a string s and an integer k, return the length of the longest substring with at most k distinct characters.
hint: Use a sliding window with a hashmap to count unique characters in current window.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(k) space.

title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
problem: Given a string s and an integer k, return the length of the longest substring containing the same letter, after replacing up to k letters.
hint: Use a sliding window, track the max frequency in current window.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(26) space.

title: Permutation in String
problem: Given two strings s1 and s2, return true if s2 contains a permutation of s1.
hint: Compare character frequency counts using a sliding window.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Find All Anagrams in a String
problem: Given a string s and a string p, return all start indices of p's anagrams in s.
hint: Sliding window with character count arrays/hashes.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Longest Substring with At Most Two Distinct Characters
problem: Given a string s, return the length of the longest substring with at most two distinct characters.
hint: Sliding window and hashmap — similar to previous K-distinct problem, set k=2.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Find All Duplicates in an Array
problem: Given an integer array nums of length n with numbers in the range 1 to n, find all elements that appear twice.
hint: Mark seen indices as negative in place.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(1) space (excluding output).

title: Find the Duplicate Number
problem: Given an array of n+1 integers where each integer is between 1 and n, find the duplicate one.
hint: Use cycle detection (Floyd's Tortoise and Hare) or binary search.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Missing Number
problem: Given an array containing n distinct numbers, return the missing number.
hint: Sum, XOR, or mark in place.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: First Missing Positive
problem: Given an unsorted integer array, find the smallest missing positive integer.
hint: Index marking: use value as index to place correct number at index, then scan.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Find Peak Element
problem: Given an input array nums, find a peak element and return its index. An element is a peak if it is greater than its neighbors.
hint: Binary search can be used since you only need to compare neighbors.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(log n) time and O(1) space.

title: Search a 2D Matrix
problem: Given an m x n matrix and a target, return true if the target exists in the matrix.
hint: Use binary search by treating the matrix as a sorted array.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(log(mn)) time and O(1) space.

title: Search a 2D Matrix II
problem: Given an m x n matrix, return true if the target exists in the matrix. Each row and column is sorted.
hint: Start from top-right, move left or down based on comparison.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(m+n) time and O(1) space.

title: Merge Sorted Array
problem: You are given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2, merge nums2 into nums1 as one sorted array in-place.
hint: Start filling nums1 from the end using two pointers.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n+m) time and O(1) space.

title: Majority Element
problem: Given an array of size n, find the majority element (> n/2 times).
hint: Voting algorithm (Boyer-Moore) or hash counting.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Majority Element II
problem: Given an array, find all elements that appear more than ⌊ n/3 ⌋ times.
hint: At most two majority elements; extend Boyer-Moore algorithm.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Excel Sheet Column Number
problem: Given a string columnTitle representing the column title as in Excel, return its corresponding column number.
hint: Treat as a number in base 26 (A=1, B=2, ...).
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Valid Number
problem: Validate if a string can be interpreted as a decimal number.
hint: Use a finite automaton or careful state simulation.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Pow(x, n)
problem: Implement pow(x, n), which calculates x raised to the power n.
hint: Exponentiation by squaring (divide and conquer recursion or loop).
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(log n) time and O(1) space.

title: Spiral Matrix II
problem: Given an integer n, generate an n x n matrix filled with elements from 1 to n^2 in spiral order.
hint: Keep track of the current bounds and fill in layers.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n^2) time and O(1) space.

title: Rotate List
problem: Given the head of a linked list, rotate the list to the right by k places.
hint: Find the length, connect end to start, break at new head.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Linked List Cycle II
problem: Given the head of a linked list, return the node where the cycle begins. If there is no cycle, return null.
hint: Use slow and fast pointers; once they meet, move from head and meeting point together.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: LRU Cache
problem: Design and implement a data structure for Least Recently Used (LRU) cache with get and put operations.
hint: Double linked list and hashmap enable O(1) operations.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(1) time and O(capacity) space per operation.

title: Min Stack
problem: Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element in constant time.
hint: Store current min for each value pushed.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(1) time and O(n) space per operation.

title: Binary Search Tree Iterator
problem: Implement an iterator for a binary search tree (BST) with next and hasNext methods.
hint: Inorder traversal using a stack.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(1) amortized time per call and O(h) space.

title: Summary Ranges
problem: Given a sorted integer array, return the smallest sorted list of ranges that cover all numbers in the array.
hint: Traverse and merge consecutive numbers into ranges.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Implement Queue using Stacks
problem: Implement a first in first out (FIFO) queue using only two stacks.
hint: Push to one stack, pop/peek from the other. Rebalance as needed.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(1) amortized time per operation.

title: Implement Stack using Queues
problem: Implement a last in first out (LIFO) stack using only two queues.
hint: Push to one queue, for pop/peek move all but one to other queue.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time for pop/peek, O(1) space.

title: Design Circular Queue
problem: Design a circular queue that supports enqueue, dequeue, front, rear, and checking if the queue is full or empty.
hint: Use an array with head, tail pointers and a size counter.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(1) time per operation.

title: Design Circular Deque
problem: Design a circular deque that supports adding and deleting elements from front or rear, checking if it's full or empty.
hint: Array with head, tail pointers, circularly increasing indices.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(1) time per operation.

title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
problem: Implement a trie with insert, search, and startsWith methods.
hint: Use a tree-like node structure for each character.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(m) time per operation, where m is the word length.

title: Add and Search Word - Data structure design
problem: Design a data structure that supports adding words and searching with '.' as wildcard.
hint: DFS for search, trie for fast prefix search.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(m) time per operation.

title: Word Dictionary
problem: Design a word dictionary that supports adding and searching with '.' as wildcard.
hint: Similar to previous, use a trie and DFS for dot searches.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(m) time per operation.

title: Implement Magic Dictionary
problem: Design a dictionary structure for searching if a word can be formed by modifying exactly one character.
hint: For each word, store all possible wildcards for one character changed.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n*m) time for build.

title: Replace Words
problem: Given a dictionary and a sentence, replace words in sentence with root of the dictionary.
hint: Use trie for fast prefix lookup.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n*m) time.

title: Find Words That Can Be Formed by Characters
problem: Given an array of words and string chars, find the sum length of words that can be formed with chars (each letter used at most once).
hint: Count chars frequency and check for each word.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(N*M) time.

title: Search Suggestions System
problem: Given an array of strings products and a string searchWord, return a list of 3 product suggestions after each character is typed. Suggestions should be sorted.
hint: Use trie + min-heap or sort & binary search for prefix matches.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n log n) time or O(nk) for trie-based, n = product count, k = searchWord length.

title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
problem: Implement addWord and searchWord methods. SearchWord may contain '.' as wildcard.
hint: Trie + DFS for searching wildcards.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(m) time per operation, m = max word length.

title: Design Search Autocomplete System
problem: Design a search autocomplete system for sentences, returning top k matching sentences for current prefix.
hint: Trie nodes store sentence frequencies.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(k) retrieval time, k = top results.

title: Longest Word in Dictionary
problem: Given a list of words, find the longest word made of other words in the list.
hint: Sort by length, use trie for prefix lookup on all substrings.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(nk) time, n = word count, k = max word length.

title: Word Break II
problem: Given a string and dictionary, return all possible sentences where each word is in the dictionary.
hint: Recursion + DP memoization for breaking sentences.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(2^n) time.

title: Palindrome Partitioning
problem: Given a string s, partition s such that every substring is a palindrome.
hint: DFS all possible partitions, check palindrome at each cut.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(2^n) time and O(n^2) for palindrome precomputation.

title: Restore IP Addresses
problem: Given a string s containing digits, return all possible valid IP address combinations.
hint: Try all splits, check validity at each step (length and value).
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(1) per answer, total O(n^3).

title: Expression Add Operators
problem: Given a string num and a target, insert operators (+,-,*) so the expression evaluates to target.
hint: DFS recursive backtracking: track current value and last used value for multiplication.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(4^n) time for n = num length.

title: Remove Invalid Parentheses
problem: Remove minimum number of parentheses to make the string valid, return all possible results.
hint: BFS and track levels, stop when first valid found.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n!) time for n = string size.

title: Generate Parentheses
problem: Given n pairs of parentheses, generate all valid combinations.
hint: Recursive backtracking – add '(' or ')' when allowed.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(2^n) time, n = number of pairs.

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
problem: Given a binary tree and two nodes, find their lowest common ancestor.
hint: Postorder DFS and look for splits from both children.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(h) space.

title: Design Twitter
problem: Design the Twitter class that supports posting tweets, retrieving the news feed, and following/unfollowing other users.
hint: Use heaps to keep a sliding window of recent tweets, plus adjacency lists.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(log n) for retrieval, where n = number of tweets.

title: Find Median from Data Stream
problem: Design a data structure that can return the median of incoming numbers in O(log n) time.
hint: Two heaps: max-heap for lower half, min-heap for upper half.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(log n) time per insert and O(1) for median.

title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)
problem: Implement a data structure that supports insert, delete, and getRandom (all O(1) average time).
hint: HashMap + ArrayList lets you swap and remove in O(1) time.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(1) for all operations.

title: LFU Cache
problem: Design and implement a data structure for Least Frequently Used (LFU) cache with O(1) get and put.
hint: Frequency table with double linked lists for each frequency, plus a hashmap.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(1) time per operation.

title: Randomized Set
problem: Design a set supporting insert, remove, and getRandom in average O(1) time.
hint: HashMap for locations, array for values.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(1) time per operation.

title: Basic Calculator
problem: Implement a basic calculator to evaluate string expressions with '+', '-', '(', ')', and non-negative integers.
hint: Use two stacks or keep a running sum and sign, process each token.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(n) space.

title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
problem: Given an array of heights, find the largest rectangle that can be formed in the histogram.
hint: Use a stack to track boundaries and compute area efficiently.
recommended_time_space: You should aim for O(n) time and O(n) space.
